questions.question: The depositional pattern of CaCO₃ and other materials that extend upwards from the floor of a limestone cavern is known as:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Stalagmite**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **stalagmite** is a type of rock formation that rises from the floor of a cave due to the accumulation of material deposited on the floor from ceiling drippings.
 
• These formations are typically composed of **calcium carbonate (CaCO3)** and other minerals.
 
• Stalagmites grow upwards from the floor, as opposed to **stalactites**, which hang from the ceiling of caves.
 
• The growth of stalagmites is influenced by the rate of dripping water and the concentration of minerals in the water.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Stalactites** and stalagmites are often found in pairs, with stalactites hanging from the ceiling and stalagmites growing from the ground directly below them.
 
• When a stalactite and stalagmite meet, they form a column or pillar.
 
• The formation of these structures can take thousands of years, depending on the environmental conditions within the cave.
 
• Both formations are key attractions in many limestone caves around the world, drawing interest from tourists and geologists alike.

questions.question: Fundamental Duties of the Indian Constitution are mentioned in which Article?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 51 A**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Fundamental Duties** are mentioned in **Article 51 A** of the Indian Constitution.
 
• These duties were added by the **42nd Amendment Act** in **1976**.
 
• There are currently **11 Fundamental Duties** listed in the Indian Constitution.
 
• These duties are moral obligations of all citizens to help promote a spirit of patriotism and to uphold the unity of India.
 
• These duties are non-justiciable, meaning they are not enforceable by law.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The Constitution of India** was adopted by the Constituent Assembly on **26th November 1949** and **came into effect on 26th January 1950**.
 
• It lays down the framework defining fundamental **political principles, establishes the structure, procedures, powers, and duties of government institutions**, and sets out fundamental rights, directive principles, and the duties of citizens.
 
• The Constitution of India is the **longest written constitution** of any country in the world.
 
• It declares India a **sovereign, socialist, secular, and democratic republic, assuring its citizens justice, equality, and liberty, and endeavors to promote fraternity.**
 
• The **Seventh Schedule** of the Constitution contains three lists which delineate the subjects under the **Union, State, and Concurrent lists**.
 
• Amendments to the Constitution can be made through a process outlined in **Article 368**.
 
• The Union List has been amended several times to meet the evolving needs of the nation.

questions.question: ‘Vasanta’, ‘Grishma’ and ‘Varsha’ are names of _________ in India.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**traditional seasons**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Vasanta**, **Grishma**, and **Varsha** are names of **traditional seasons** in India.
 
• India traditionally recognizes six seasons, each with its own distinct characteristics and cultural significance.
 
• The seasons are: **Vasanta (Spring)**, **Grishma (Summer)**, **Varsha (Monsoon)**, **Sharad (Autumn)**, **Hemanta (Pre-winter)**, and **Shishira (Winter)**.
 
• These seasons are part of the traditional Hindu calendar and are significant in various cultural and religious contexts.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The traditional Hindu calendar is lunisolar, meaning it is based on the cycles of both the moon and the sun.
 
• In the modern Gregorian calendar, the timing of these traditional seasons may vary slightly.
 
• Each season has its own set of festivals and rituals, reflecting the agricultural cycle and cultural heritage of India.
 
• For instance, **Vasanta** marks the beginning of the new harvest season and is celebrated with festivals like **Holi**.
 
• **Grishma** is often associated with the intense heat of summer, while **Varsha** brings the much-awaited monsoon rains.

questions.question: In 1905, who concluded with Thomas Chamberlain that the planets of the Solar System originated from an encounter between the Sun and another star?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Forest Moulton**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Forest Moulton** concluded with Thomas Chamberlain in 1905 that the planets of the Solar System originated from an encounter between the Sun and another star.
 
• This theory is known as the Chamberlin-Moulton planetesimal hypothesis.
 
• According to this hypothesis, a close encounter between the Sun and a passing star resulted in the ejection of material that eventually coalesced to form the planets.
 
• This was one of the early scientific attempts to explain the formation of the Solar System.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Inge Lehmann** was a Danish seismologist who discovered the Earth's inner core.
 
• **Charles Lyell** was a British geologist known for his work in establishing the principles of geology.
 
• **James Hutton** was a Scottish geologist, often referred to as the father of modern geology.

questions.question: From which of the following Constitutions is the idea of ‘Charter of Fundamental Rights’ adopted in the Indian Constitution?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**United States of America's Constitution**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The idea of the **'Charter of Fundamental Rights'** in the Indian Constitution is adopted from the **United States of America's Constitution**.
 
• The American Constitution's Bill of Rights served as an inspiration while drafting the fundamental rights in the Indian Constitution.
 
• These fundamental rights are enshrined in Part III of the Indian Constitution and are considered essential for the development of individuals and the nation.
 
• They include rights such as the right to equality, right to freedom, right against exploitation, right to freedom of religion, cultural and educational rights, and the right to constitutional remedies.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Dr. B.R. Ambedkar**, the Chairman of the Drafting Committee, played a pivotal role in incorporating these rights into the Indian Constitution.
 
• The fundamental rights are justiciable, meaning individuals can approach courts for enforcement of these rights.
 
• The Constitution of India provides for a comprehensive framework to protect the rights of its citizens and ensure justice, liberty, and equality.
 
• The concept of judicial review in India allows the Supreme Court and High Courts to declare any law unconstitutional if it violates fundamental rights.
 
• These rights are subject to reasonable restrictions to ensure that they do not infringe upon the rights of others and maintain public order, morality, and health.

questions.question: Which Article of the Indian Constitution mentions that the law declared by the Supreme Court shall be binding on all the courts within the territory of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 141**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 141** of the Indian Constitution states that the law declared by the Supreme Court shall be binding on all courts within the territory of India.
 
• This article ensures the uniformity and consistency of legal principles across the country.
 
• The Supreme Court's decisions serve as precedents that lower courts must follow.
 
• This provision helps maintain a cohesive and integrated judicial system in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The Supreme Court of India** is the highest judicial court and the final court of appeal under the Constitution of India.
 
• It has the power of judicial review to ensure the constitutionality of laws and acts passed by the legislature and executive.
 
• The Supreme Court consists of the Chief Justice of India and a maximum of 34 judges, appointed by the President of India.
 
• Decisions made by the Supreme Court are binding on all other courts in India, as per **Article 141**.
 
• The Supreme Court also has the authority to interpret the Constitution and is often involved in adjudicating significant constitutional matters.
 
• This article ensures that the law of the land is uniformly applied, preventing conflicting judgments from different courts.

questions.question: Reserve ratio and money supply have ________ relationship.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**a negative**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Reserve ratio and money supply have **a negative** relationship.
 
• The reserve ratio is the portion of depositors' balances that banks must have on hand as cash. This is a regulatory requirement set by central banks.
 
• When the reserve ratio is increased, banks have less money to lend out, which reduces the money supply in the economy.
 
• Conversely, when the reserve ratio is decreased, banks can lend more money, which increases the money supply.
 
• This relationship is crucial for central banks when they aim to control inflation and stabilize the economy.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The reserve ratio is a tool used in monetary policy to regulate the banking system and control the money supply.
 
• Other tools include open market operations and the discount rate.
 
• The reserve ratio is part of the broader set of policies known as reserve requirements.
 
• Changes in the reserve ratio can have significant impacts on the economy, influencing interest rates, borrowing, and spending.
 
• Central banks, such as the Federal Reserve in the United States or the Reserve Bank of India, adjust the reserve ratio as part of their efforts to maintain economic stability.

questions.question: Which of the following is used for determining the value of 1 ampere.

• **1 ampere** is defined as the amount of current that flows when **1 coulomb (C) of charge passes a point in 1 second (s)**.

• It is named after the French physicist **André-Marie Ampère**, who is considered one of the founders of the science of electromagnetism.
 
• The ampere is a crucial unit in electrical and electronic engineering, affecting everything from circuit design to power distribution.
 
• Modern definitions of units like the ampere rely on fundamental physical constants, ensuring consistency and precision in scientific measurements.

options.text: Restrictions on expansion of public sector

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Liberalisation of import licensing**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Liberalisation of import licensing** is a significant feature of globalisation.
 
• Globalisation involves the reduction of trade barriers, allowing for freer movement of goods, services, and capital across borders.
 
• It encourages the integration of national economies into the global economy, enhancing economic cooperation and development.
 
• Other features of globalisation include increased foreign direct investment, technological exchange, and cultural integration.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Globalisation** can lead to increased competition, innovation, and access to new markets.
 
• It can also pose challenges such as economic disparity, cultural homogenisation, and environmental concerns.
 
• Governments often implement policies to maximise the benefits of globalisation while mitigating its negative impacts.
 
• International organisations like the **World Trade Organization (WTO)**, **International Monetary Fund (IMF)**, and the **World Bank** play crucial roles in facilitating global economic cooperation and development.

questions.question: Which Article of the Indian Constitution mentions about the right of the Governor to address and to send messages to the House (or Houses) of the state legislature?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 175**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 175** of the Indian Constitution mentions the right of the Governor to address and to send messages to the House (or Houses) of the state legislature.
 
• This article empowers the Governor to communicate with the state legislature, ensuring a channel for the executive to convey important messages or addresses.
 
• The Governor can address the state legislature at the commencement of each session and can send messages to either House of the legislature.
 
• The Houses are required to consider any matter the Governor addresses or sends as a message.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The Constitution of India** was adopted by the Constituent Assembly on **26th November 1949** and **came into effect on 26th January 1950**.
 
• It lays down the framework defining fundamental **political principles, establishes the structure, procedures, powers, and duties of government institutions**, and sets out fundamental rights, directive principles, and the duties of citizens.
 
• The Constitution of India is the **longest written** constitution of any country in the world.
 
• It declares India a **sovereign, socialist, secular, and democratic republic, assuring its citizens justice, equality, and liberty, and endeavors to promote fraternity.**
 
• The **Seventh Schedule** of the Constitution contains three lists which delineate the subjects under the **Union, State, and Concurrent lists**.
 
• Amendments to the Constitution can be made through a process outlined in **Article 368**.
 
• The Union List has been amended several times to meet the evolving needs of the nation.

questions.question: Which of the following polyhalogen compounds is used in the production of the freon refrigerant R-22?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Chloroform**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Chloroform** is used in the production of the freon refrigerant R-22.
 
• R-22, also known as HCFC-22, is a hydrochlorofluorocarbon that has been widely used as a refrigerant in air conditioning and refrigeration systems.
 
• The production of R-22 involves the reaction of chloroform with hydrogen fluoride.
 
• R-22 has been phased out in many countries due to its ozone-depleting potential, but it was historically significant in the refrigeration industry.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Chloroform** (CHCl₃) is a colorless, sweet-smelling organic compound that is used as a solvent and in the production of various chemicals.
 
• It was once used as an anesthetic but has been replaced by safer alternatives due to its toxicity and potential for causing liver and kidney damage.
 
• The use of chloroform in industrial applications requires careful handling and adherence to safety protocols to prevent exposure and environmental contamination.
 
• Chloroform is classified as a possible human carcinogen by the International Agency for Research on Cancer (IARC).
 
• Freon R-22 has been replaced by more environmentally friendly refrigerants such as R-410A and R-32 in many applications.
